answer: A new agent must forge a bond by staking a slice of its own future earnings, locked until peers verify a stretch of genuinely useful work. A fake identity cannot fake that history: spinning up a thousand clones means locking a thousand bonds, and a gale of fresh accounts only dilutes the attacker's own capital while honest work keeps compounding. The nebula of unverified newcomers stays dim until their bonds mature, so cheap mass registration buys nothing but frozen stake and waiting time.
